metadata.title: sentient-rs TMS Component Definition — MIL-STD-3071 Catalog Mapping
metadata.remarks: Maps sentient-rs components (the descriptor-factory codegen tool, the bin-rpi runtime, the lib-schema wire types, the lib-mapping transform) to the compliance/oscal/catalog.json controls. Each implemented-requirement's `implementation-status` prop uses: implemented | partial | planned | alternative-implementation | not-applicable. Lula 1 is vendor-abandoned (not depended on); the `conftest-policy` link rel is this project's own convention for ‘which Rego policy machine-checks this requirement’, playing the role Lula's validation links played, without depending on Lula's schema.

components.title: tms-idl-codegen (MIL-STD-3071 descriptor factory)
components.description: Host-only codegen tool, its own Cargo workspace (tools/tms-idl-codegen), excluded from the firmware/cargo-vet surface.

components.title: lib-schema (TMS wire type definitions)
components.description: Schema-shape layer only — no transport, no runtime wiring.
components.purpose: Hand-authored + descriptor-factory-verified Rust structs/enums mirroring the IDL field shape, @key/@optional/@range/@unit annotations.

control-implementations.description: Mapping of lib-schema (TMS wire type definitions) to the MIL-STD-3071 topic conformance catalog.

implemented-requirements.description: Every IDL @key field is a distinct Rust field; tms-coverage.json's per-type `keys` count is the machine-readable evidence.

links.text: tms-coverage.md ‘Types with units / ranges’ table (@key column)

implemented-requirements.description: IDL @range/@min/@max annotations are captured in the generated catalogue (tms-coverage.json `ranges` count); runtime enforcement that populated values stay in-range is not independently machine-tested by this gate.

links.text: tms-coverage.md ‘Types with units / ranges’ table (@range column)

implemented-requirements.description: All @unit-annotated fields spot-checked correct against the IDL (p.u. SoC, degC, s, V/A/W, W/s); tms-coverage.json `units` count per type is the machine-readable evidence of annotation presence.

links.text: tms-coverage.md ‘Types with units / ranges’ table (@unit column)

implemented-requirements.description: No DDS-XTypes wire exists in this project (JSON has no FINAL/APPENDABLE/MUTABLE byte); the analogous concern (additive-only field evolution) is tracked informally, not machine-checked.

links.text: §7.1 transport adaptation

implemented-requirements.description: NaN-for-unavailable and IDL enum wire spellings (#[serde(rename = "IDL_SPELLING")]) are implemented; DiagnosticTroubleCode.occurrenceCount is hardcoded 1 (no edge-triggered tracking) and severity is uniformly Major (over-signals lesser faults) — documented simplifications, not regressions.

components.title: lib-mapping (Seplos/Voltronic canonical → TMS transform)
components.purpose: Maps CanonicalReading/CanonicalInverterReading onto TMS struct instances and builds MQTT topic strings.

control-implementations.description: Mapping of lib-mapping (Seplos/Voltronic canonical → TMS transform) to the MIL-STD-3071 topic conformance catalog.

implemented-requirements.description: `sink.rs::topic_into` builds `tms/{device_id}/{snake_slug}` from the CamelCase TMS type name — a documented, reversible bridge rule.

links.text: §6 topic name / transport mapping

implemented-requirements.description: Sign inversion (Seplos charge-positive -> TMS source-positive) and unit scaling (centi-volts/-amps, millivolts, deci-Kelvin, deci-percent) are documented, load-bearing conventions at transform.rs's call sites.
